title: Relief map of Greece
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y5 lesson 11 (Relief map of Greece (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 11: Greece's physical features. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: A mountainous land
points: Most of Greece is mountains or hills
Pindus mountains run north to south

panels.title: A long coastline
points: Nowhere is very far from the sea

model.title: Why do most Greeks live near the coast?

parts.text: Mountains are steep and hard to farm
Coasts have flat land and harbours
So towns grew by the sea

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Flat land, trade and fishing draw people to the coast

blocks.text: Shade the high mountains brown, lower hills orange and lowland green, using the relief map on the slides.

keywords.def: a natural part of the land
the edge where land meets sea
a large area of flat land

questions.q: How much higher is Mount Olympus than Ben Nevis?

questions.a: Mountains made travel by land hard

questions.q: Core: On a relief map, shade mountains, mark Mount Olympus, two plains and three coastal cities, then write two sentences about where people live.
questions.a: Accurate map and sentences linking land and settlement

questions.q: Extend: Compare Greece's landscape with the UK's.
questions.a: Both have mountains and long coasts; Greece is more mountainous and has more islands

questions.q: Stretch: How might the mountains have helped Greek city-states stay independent?
questions.a: Hard for armies to cross, so each city could defend itself
B) Mount Olympus. Mount Olympus is about 2,918 metres high.

questions.q: Big question: how do mountains and sea shape where people live?
questions.a: People settle on flat coasts and plains with harbours and farmland; few live in high mountains
